synopsis: Northern Ireland requires separate regulatory treatment under the Windsor Framework because EU product law applies there [f2223, f15494]. The glossary contrasts this with Great Britain’s parallel UKCA mark and approved bodies [f15110]. Accordingly, planners should not assume that a single Great Britain declaration route covers both Great Britain and Northern Ireland [f2224, f15494]. The chapter recommendation and glossary agree on this distinction, but the supplied facts do not specify the declaration route required for Northern Ireland [f2223, f2224, f15494, f15110].

relations.note: Both identify EU product law under Windsor as requiring distinct Northern Ireland treatment.
Both warn against assuming one declaration route covers Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
Contrasting regulatory regimes support separate treatment for Northern Ireland.
Different product-law regimes justify caution about a shared declaration route.
Northern Ireland’s EU-law treatment explains the warning about Great Britain declarations.
